title: ICE wants AI to take on more of its legal workload
summary: The agency is looking for software that can help its attorneys manage the growing demands of litigation, investigations and other legal matters.

title: ‘A rushed and complicated system.’ Federal employees say they’re in the dark over limited top ratings
summary: A mandate to limit outstanding performance scores has managers playing a numbers game and risks pitting teammates against each other.

title: Oversight of nuclear material security cut back due to civil service reductions, GAO finds
summary: The Government Accountability Office also reported that the National Nuclear Security Administration has more than lost its recent hiring gains.

title: State Department orders ‘super intelligence’ wording across all official communications
summary: An internal cable from the agency extends Trump’s terminology change to emails, speeches, websites and official titles, while preserving legal language and historical records.

title: Trump’s IG pick at the VA is ‘watering down’ oversight, some employees allege
summary: As the Veterans Affairs inspector general faces mounting workforce challenges, some employees and former watchdogs raise questions about the office's trajectory.

title: Union seeks new avenue to restore VA contract
summary: The American Federation of Government Employees asked a federal judge to issue an “indicative” ruling that would only take effect if OKed by the First Circuit Court of Appeals.

title: This cybersecurity agency is supposed to protect U.S. elections. Officials fear it’s been compromised by Trump
summary: President Donald Trump’s 2027 budget proposal would reduce funding for the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency by another $700 million, which could necessitate 900 additional layoffs.

title: Senator warns hundreds of federal web addresses may lack key spying protection
summary: The list includes websites for FBI tips, intelligence job applications and the Veterans Crisis Line.

title: Enforcement ‘surge’ from DOJ, IRS uncovers $490M in suspected tax fraud
summary: Justice and IRS officials said this won’t be the last tax fraud enforcement surge of its kind. But it's not yet clear how much money they'll claw back from suspected fraudsters.

title: Judge again orders reinstatement of Bureau of Prisons union contracts, but stops short of contempt
summary: U.S. District Judge Jordan Oliver found that the agency’s re-termination of its collective bargaining agreements last week violated last month’s preliminary injunction but said he would not police individual contract infractions.

title: VA allows union contract to expire for most employees
summary: Individuals hired as departmental police officers, firefighters and security guards, exempted from Trump’s anti-union orders, remain covered under the expired collective bargaining agreement, albeit only for “mandatory” conditions of employment.

title: USPS ‘ready to deliver’ ballots in midterms without mail-in voting EO restrictions
summary: The Postal Service's law enforcement agency is investigating suspicious letters sent to several state officials who oversee election operations.

title: CMS hopes to quadruple provider suspensions over next 6 months, official says
summary: A new exclusion authority is the Trump administration’s latest step in a technology-enabled drive to restrict fraud, waste and abuse.

title: HUD’s staffing cuts hurt certain housing services, watchdog finds
summary: Housing organizations told the Government Accountability Office that they now face more obstacles getting in touch with department employees in a timely manner.

title: AI offers Secret Service unique mission enhancements, official says
summary: Threats against the Secret Service’s full-time protectees are up over 40% since last year. The service’s CIO and CAIO Chris Kraft said AI “can help us as we investigate those threats, monitor those threats [and] bring together correlations between seemingly disparate information.”

title: Federal retirees face more than a COLA change in 2027
summary: From Medicare premiums and Social Security earnings limits to a federal pay freeze, several changes could affect retirees’ finances and the benefits available to them next year.

title: The next counterintelligence threat may be hiding in federal hiring
summary: COMMENTARY | Foreign adversaries are exploiting resumes, recruiting and professional relationships to pursue sensitive information. Federal agencies need to recognize the risks without making it harder to recruit the talent they need.

title: OPM revamps online pay tables, spearheads AI adoption across federal workforce
summary: The agency's CIO Adam Starr described the pay table refresh as part of a broader plan to “make every part of the federal experience tech-first."

title: Trump quietly hired political appointees under a new job classification, good government group reports
summary: While Schedule G is not officially set up in regulation, the Office of Personnel Management emphasized that the position category for political appointees was established by executive order and that the agency issued implementing guidance.

title: Cost-of-living adjustments for federal retirees to increase next year
summary: Former federal workers are set to receive between 2.6% and 3.6% more from their retirement annuity next year, according to new numbers from the Social Security Administration.

title: ICE resists automatic activation of body cameras despite oversight concerns
summary: Federal investigators found gaps in guidance for immigration officers’ use of body-worn cameras, raising concerns about whether the agencies can ensure the devices are used as required.

title: A judge just put USDA’s employee relocation plans on ice
summary: The order blocks the department from moving about 2,600 employees or closing affected offices while a legal challenge to its reorganization proceeds.

title: Disability accommodations at Labor get extra scrutiny with annual reviews
summary: The department plans to review existing accommodations for disabilities and pregnancy-related conditions, with employees potentially asked to provide updated medical documentation.

title: Fraud-prevention work stalled at USDA amid staffing cuts and funding disputes
summary: Federal officials have identified ways to curb theft of SNAP benefits, but staffing losses, funding decisions and congressional inaction have slowed efforts to protect recipients.

title: Labor has mostly stopped checking whether federal contractors are following disability rules
summary: A watchdog found that the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs has no plans to restart routine audits, leaving less oversight of protections for workers with disabilities.
